title: Monitoring, delayed labels and online experiments
outcome: Monitor mature cohorts and service behavior without confusing delayed outcomes or changing traffic with model improvement.

exercises.title: Report immature labels
exercises.task: Evaluate the two requests at day 2.
exercises.hint: Use the same eligible cohort in both denominators.
exercises.answer: The missing failure label has not become a success. The report must expose incomplete outcome ascertainment.

exercises.title: Wait for the cohort
exercises.task: Evaluate the same requests at day 10.
exercises.hint: No model change is required for the apparent decline.
exercises.answer: The difference is explained by label arrival, so an unqualified early-versus-late accuracy comparison is misleading.

exercises.title: Identical distributions
exercises.hint: Every log ratio is 1 before taking the logarithm.
exercises.answer: This is an exact diagnostic invariant, not proof that model quality is unchanged.

exercises.title: Disjoint support
exercises.hint: Both are compared to their midpoint.
exercises.answer: The finite maximum is a useful boundary test and differs from an unbounded one-direction KL divergence.

exercises.title: Choose assignment units
exercises.task: Requests from one user share conversational history.
exercises.expected: Consider user-level assignment and cluster-aware analysis.
exercises.hint: Interference can occur across request rows.
exercises.answer: The experimental unit should reflect how exposure and outcomes can influence one another; many rows do not create independent users.

exercises.title: Investigate an alert
exercises.task: A drift score rises while mature-cohort quality is stable.
exercises.expected: Investigate composition and coverage before concluding model degradation.
exercises.hint: A diagnostic is not a causal attribution.
exercises.answer: A changed input mix may be benign or may reveal unsupported future risk; retain outcome and operational evidence alongside drift.
